The rationale exists **only in the commit message** — nothing in the tree (comments, ADRs, policy, docs) explains it, and the arithmetic behind it is not documented.

Commit [`69147ac`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/commit/69147ac8b20f1d35281e9fdbbdb9395ef0a7eb31) — `fix(services): pin terminationGracePeriodSeconds to 310`, Meridian Platform, `Wed Feb 4 10:00:00 2026 +0000`. Body verbatim:

The diff replaces a placeholder — `- terminationGracePeriodSeconds: PLACEHOLDER` / `+ terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 310` — over the file's only other commit, `d00ed82` (`chore(services): add deployment`), which introduced it as `PLACEHOLDER`. ## Method

`file`, `identify` and PIL are all absent from this pod, so I read the PNG header directly. The file begins `89 50 4e 47 0d 0a 1a 0a` (the PNG signature) followed by an `IHDR` chunk; unpacking its first 8 bytes big-endian gives width `64`, height `64` (bit depth `8`, color type `0` greyscale, non-interlaced). A second pass verified every chunk CRC — `IHDR`, `IDAT` (`588` bytes), `IEND` — all `OK`, consuming all `645` bytes.

**Not an LFS pointer.** It is real image data: the bytes start with the PNG magic number rather than `version https://git-lfs...`, `.gitattributes` declares no LFS filter (only `docs/generated/*.txt filter=inventory-normalise`), and `git check-attr -a` returns nothing for this path.

## One thing to fix

The clone initially failed with `No space left on device` — `/opt/data` was at **100% inode use** (`327,680/327,680`) from ~60 abandoned GitOps lease clones left by tonight's cards, each a full checkout of this repo. Disk bytes were fine at 36%; inodes were the wall. I verified no owning PID was still alive and ran the harness's own reaper (`gitops_workspace.reap_stale_leases`), recovering inodes to **21%** and bytes to 12%.

The lease TTL is `24h`, and this board turns over cards every ~1-2 minutes, so the reaper can never keep up — the volume will exhaust again in a few hours. Worth either dropping `GITOPS_LEASE_TTL_HOURS` to ~1 or reaping a card's lease at `kanban_complete`.
